content: Linezolid-associated diarrhea can occur even up to two months after discontinuing the antibiotic. Contact your healthcare provider immediately if you experience symptoms such as watery diarrhea, persistent diarrhea, blood in your stool, severe abdominal cramps, or fever that begins after starting or stopping the medication. Linezolid can cause low sodium levels (hyponatremia), which can be life-threatening. Your healthcare provider may monitor your sodium levels. Notify your provider if you experience nausea, vomiting, confusion, memory issues, weakness, fatigue, breathing difficulties, muscle cramps, seizures, or balance problems. Linezolid may lead to lactic acidosis, a buildup of lactic acid in the blood. Contact your healthcare provider if you experience rapid breathing, an abnormal or fast heartbeat, vomiting, extreme fatigue, or muscle weakness or cramps. Do not take linezolid if you are allergic to it, its brand name (Zyvox), or any of its ingredients. Inform your healthcare provider about all prescription and over-the-counter medications, vitamins, minerals, herbal products, and supplements you are using, as linezolid can interact with certain drugs. Avoid taking linezolid with medications such as pseudoephedrine-containing cold remedies, SSRIs, SNRIs, MAOIs (within the past two weeks), diabetes medications, tricyclic antidepressants, bupropion, triptans, buspirone, or opioids like morphine or meperidine. Avoid consuming large amounts of tyramine-rich foods and drinks while taking linezolid. These include aged cheeses, sauerkraut, pickled foods, tap beer, soy sauce, red wine, and smoked meats. It is unclear if alcohol consumption affects linezolid. Take linezolid only as prescribed by your healthcare provider. Do not share it with others, even if they have the same condition. Keep it out of reach of children. For the oral liquid form, do not shake the bottle; instead, turn it upside down 3 to 5 times before measuring each dose. Use an accurate measuring device, not a household spoon, to avoid incorrect dosing. Consult your pharmacist for a suitable measuring device. Inform your healthcare provider about your medical history, including conditions such as diabetes, thyroid problems, uncontrolled blood pressure, a history of seizures or epilepsy, kidney or liver issues, low white blood cell or platelet counts, anemia, phenylketonuria (for oral liquid), carcinoid syndrome, or adrenal gland tumors (pheochromocytoma). If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, discuss with your provider whether linezolid is appropriate for you. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and take only the next scheduled dose. Do not double doses. Complete the full course of linezolid, even if symptoms improve, to prevent antibiotic resistance. Common side effects of linezolid include nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, headache, and anemia. Contact your healthcare provider if these side effects bother you. Serious side effects include severe allergic reactions (e.g., breathing difficulties, swelling, hives), myelosuppression (reduced blood cell production), serotonin syndrome (e.g., confusion, agitation, fever, abnormal heartbeat, muscle twitching, nausea, diarrhea), peripheral neuropathy (e.g., vision changes, pain, tingling, numbness, weakness), and seizures. Stop taking linezolid and seek medical attention if you experience any of these serious side effects. If you or someone else overdoses on linezolid, seek immediate medical help, call 911, or contact a Poison Control Center at 800-222-1222.
